analysis.title: European Morning Note
key_insights: US stocks surged Wednesday after Democratic midterm wins raised hopes the Iran War could end soon, which pushed oil lower. S&P 500 +1.6%, Nasdaq +0.9%, VIX near 17.
Tech megacaps rose on a bet that a Democratic-controlled Congress will force companies to cut AI spending. Amazon and Microsoft each rose more than 6%, and the Magnificent Seven basket gained 2.2%.
S&P 500 Energy Index fell 4.8%, its worst session since April 2025, tracking oil lower. Brent futures dropped 10% to below $100 a barrel.
Asia sold off in the overnight session: Kospi -6% and TAIEX -3%, with evidence of broad de-grossing across the APAC AI supply chain. Nasdaq futures were -1.4% and S&P futures -0.3%.
Qualcomm fell 7.2% after hours after guiding December quarter EPS below consensus on a broad-based rise in costs. The desk reads this as negative for handset OEMs such as MediaTek and AAC.
China is the beneficiary of rotation after the midterms: HSTECH +5%, H shares +3%, following KWEB +4.5% in the US session.
The London ETD sales desk saw a barrage of buying from the European open, with buyers in good size in CAC and OMX, continued buyers of MES (EM), and later buyers of Euro Banks (SX7E) to sell VGZ6.
Euro Stoxx 50 futures (VGZ6) were +0.4% in early trading.
